purpose: Assess a voucher-linked North Luzon fish barcode dataset and its specimen tables without transferring market or unmatched locality records to individual waterbodies.

source.citation: Dimaquibo, A. C., Jhuang, W.-C., Huang, W.-C., Encarnacion, A. B., Villarao, M. C., Yutuc, R. V., & Liao, T.-Y. (2025). DNA Barcoding of Teleost Fishes from North Luzon, Philippines: A Dataset for Ichthyofaunal Diversity Assessment. Scientific Data, 12, 1571. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-05758-3
source.coverage: Aurora, Cagayan and Zambales, Luzon; 27 sampling sites across market/landing areas and rivers.
publishedDataPaths: The article says GenBank sequences are deposited under BioProjects PRJNA1294862 and PRJNA1294866.
The publisher provides a supplementary XLSX with Tables S1a–S1c and specimen-level catalog numbers, species, sampling areas, dates, methods, accessions and status fields.
The main article's Table 1 lists ten Cagayan collection-site labels; its Buguey row is labeled only ‘Buguey’ and classified as ‘river’.
source.license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) for the article. The supplementary tables and underlying GenBank metadata require separate field-level review before reuse.

bugueySiteLead.interpretationLimit: The main article labels the site ‘Buguey’ and classifies it as a river, but no Cagayan specimen row in the supplementary XLSX uses Buguey as its sampling-area label. The article does not name the watercourse in that row or identify it as Buguey Lagoon. Do not join taxa to this site, map it to a named river or lagoon, or use its published point as a waterbody boundary without author clarification.

evidenceQualityAndScope: This is a specimen-based DNA barcoding data descriptor that combines fish purchased from markets/landing areas with fish collected from rivers. The market-catch specimens are not local wild-occurrence records for their market coordinates.

The article reports 323 species across three provinces. Its supplementary XLSX contains specimen-level species and sampling-area fields for Cagayan, Aurora and Zambales. The Cagayan sheet has river and market/landing records, with collection method recorded separately; no Cagayan row is labeled Buguey, so the main article's Buguey site cannot be linked to a fish record from this supplement.
The main article identifies 15 freshwater river sites across the three provinces and ten Cagayan sites, but does not establish the completeness of any province or river checklist.
The paper says 11 specimens remain genus-only because of identification or reference limitations. Those labels cannot be promoted to species-level claims.

The article reports voucher specimens and molecular/morphological validation. These are stronger identification sources than unlabeled market terms, but a taxon still must be joined to its specimen and collection locality before a site claim is made.

accessReview.fullArticle: Publisher-hosted PDF reviewed for the abstract, Table 1, methods, Data Records and license statement.
accessReview.supplementaryTables: Publisher-hosted XLSX retrieved and reviewed in read-only mode. It contains Tables S1a–S1c, organized by Cagayan, Aurora and Zambales, with specimen catalog, species, sampling area, date, field number, collection method and accession/status columns. No Cagayan record has a sampling-area value containing ‘Buguey’; generic or differently named river rows are not reassigned to the main-table Buguey point.
accessReview.genbank: The article lists two BioProjects. A read-only NCBI lookup confirmed the first BioProject and that a sample accession links to it, but GenBank records inspected here did not expose the site crosswalk; no accession-to-Buguey assignment was made.
accessReview.licenseLimit: The article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Do not redistribute an adapted species-by-site dataset from the paper or its supplement without explicit permission; record only source metadata and research leads pending review.

followUp: Ask the corresponding author to reconcile the main-table ‘Buguey’ river site with the supplementary tables: no Cagayan specimen row uses Buguey as its sampling-area label. Ask whether the site produced no sequenced specimens or whether its samples were recorded under another area label, and request a documented site-to-catalog/accession crosswalk.

Before any external redistribution or app use, obtain a rights decision for the supplementary tables and underlying data; the article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and no derived species-by-site table is published in Bangwit.

If reuse is explicitly authorized, crosswalk only the documented voucher/accession records to the article's actual collection site, field date, specimen ID, method and taxonomic name; keep market/landing purchases separate from river collections.

Resolve whether the source-reported Buguey river point identifies a named watercourse, then validate the site against authoritative hydrography and administrative geography. Do not equate it to Buguey Lagoon from municipality name alone.
Retain genus-only or taxonomically disputed specimens at their documented rank; independently reconcile species names against an accepted authority before any future app admission.
Obtain a publication and derivative-data rights decision before placing specimen-level taxa or metadata in Bangwit's public source/data package.

sources.supports: Peer-reviewed voucher-linked barcode dataset and publisher supplement, North Luzon scope, 2023 sampling periods, mixed market/river sampling design, Cagayan site labels, specimen-table fields, GenBank project links and CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 article terms.
NCBI BioProject cited by the paper for deposited barcode sequences; no site-specific Buguey accession was identified.
Second NCBI BioProject cited by the paper; no site-specific Buguey accession was identified.
